note: sim = this simulation; published = the named source. status says whether the figure was calibrated to, predicted, or only bounded.

sound_peak_reduction_1m_side.source: Lobarinas, Scott, Spankovich and Le Prell (2016), Int. J. Audiology 55 (S1): nine AR-15 rifles, 14 suppressors, 1 m left of the muzzle per MIL-STD-1474D; range as summarised in Murphy et al., "Developing a method to assess noise reduction of firearm suppressors for small-caliber weapons" (NIOSH/CDC stacks 221679)
sound_peak_reduction_1m_side.status: calibration target (clip_factor solved for the 22.5 dB midpoint); with clip_factor = 1 the model gives 15.4 dB

sound_peak_reduction_shooter_ear.source: Murphy, Flamme, Campbell, Zechmann, Tasko, Lankford, Meinke, Finan and Stewart (2018), Int. J. Audiology 57 (S1): peak reduction at the shooter's ear, several firearms (abstract)
sound_peak_reduction_shooter_ear.status: calibration target (dipole_share solved for the 20.5 dB midpoint); an omnidirectional source gives 14.9 dB, the full compact dipole 50.0 dB

sound_peak_reduction_behind.source: Murphy et al. (2018): instructor position about 1 m behind the shooter (abstract)
sound_peak_reduction_behind.status: prediction once the two sound parameters are set; the bare reference here is the HK416 directivity law extrapolated to 180 degrees

suppressed_level_at_ear.published: most suppressed AR-15 conditions 140 to 150 dB at the ear; above 140 dB at the right ear
suppressed_level_at_ear.source: Lobarinas et al. (2016), abstract and the Student Academy of Audiology summary
suppressed_level_at_ear.status: follows from the ear calibration; the model has no ejection-port or gas-vent source, which is what the paper blames for the right ear, so it sits below the measured band

supersonic_crack.sim: N-wave entries untouched: 149.0 dB at the down-range listener, bare and suppressed
supersonic_crack.published: a suppressor does not affect the ballistic shock of a supersonic bullet
supersonic_crack.source: physics (Whitham 1952 N-wave depends on the bullet alone); assets/hk416/sound section 2

first_round_pop.published: no controlled 5.56 figure found; trade sources give 5 to 10 dB in general and "little difference" on short 5.56 rifles
first_round_pop.source: The Truth About Guns, "The science of silence" (general estimate); RECOIL, best 5.56 suppressors (5.56 remark). Neither is a measurement report

heat_per_shot.published: 7 to 10 F (3.9 to 5.6 K) per round, rule of thumb; 100 rounds raise the core about 750 F (4.2 K per round)
heat_per_shot.source: retailer rule of thumb (Silencer Central and others, no method given); Small Arms Defense Journal (100-round burst figure, as found by search; article not read in full)
heat_per_shot.status: prediction with an inferred Stanton number (not fitted)

heat_100_rounds.source: Small Arms Defense Journal, as above

back_pressure.published: M4A1 (direct impingement) with a suppressor: about 25 % more bolt carrier speed; patents cite 20 to 30 % more rate of fire. No HK416 figure found; the manual gives 700 to 900 rpm for the bare rifle
back_pressure.source: NDIA 2016 Armament Systems Forum briefing 18366 (Davis), slide figure; US patents 10151544 and 11578931 (inventors' statements)
back_pressure.status: prediction. The HK416 short-stroke piston vents after 3 mm, so the gas system itself adds little; residual bore pressure first grips the case harder (slower without the thrust term), then pushes on the case head

recoil.status: prediction; the same blowdown scale as the HK416 action is applied to the exit thrust

blast_scaling_cross_check.note: Fansler and Schmidt scale peak overpressure with (energy efflux rate)^0.55. Applied to the can it gives the reduction the exit flow would have if it started as abruptly as a bare muzzle: a lower bound on the reduction.
blast_scaling_cross_check.source: Fansler and Schmidt (1983), BRL-TR-2504 (exponent recalled, not re-read)

bare_equivalence.status: consistency check of core.py against assets/hk416/action

energy_bare_J.note: the unaccounted part is the enthalpy of the 6.1 mg breech leak, which is not tallied

geometry.published: fielded 5.56 QD cans: about 6 to 7 in long, 1.5 in diameter, 14 to 22 oz
geometry.source: makers' published specifications in general (class figures, recalled; no single product)
